correctness.rationale: Every nonempty self-inverse restriction is invariant under a global dihedral involution. Explicit cycle structures give invariant-domain polynomials, and agreement sets of distinct dihedral permutations show the sole nonidentity duplicate is a swapped antipodal pair in even length. Verified by exact direct maps for n=3..10; finite checks corroborate, not replace, the general argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The known total monoid cardinality and minimal generating rank do not imply the count of self-inverse elements in each domain rank. A general restriction-semigroup theorem might subsume the orbit-count proof; none was established in the checked material.

originality.rationale: Fernandes–Paulista (arXiv:2205.02196) already prove the rank-two antipodal nonunique-extension lemma and the monoid presentation, while Dimitrova et al. (arXiv:2301.01519) give counts for related submonoids. Neither inspected paper supplies a self-inverse restriction polynomial; the new count combines invariant-domain orbit polynomials with the acknowledged prior collision lemma. No stronger covering result was identified, but priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: A complete natural algebraic rank distribution of self-inverse elements for the full family of dihedral inverse monoids, including the subtle even-length antipodal restriction collision. The exact polynomial explains a sharp binomial rank law and exponential dominance of idempotents, distinct from previously studied total sizes and semigroup ranks.
